title: Trane Furnace Code 2 Flashes: External Lockout
meaning: An external safety device locked the furnace out.
diySteps: Check that all access panels are secure.
Allow the unit to cool before resetting.
whenToCallPro: External lockouts require identifying which safety device opened.

title: Trane Furnace Code 3 Flashes: Pressure Switch Error
meaning: The pressure switch circuit failed during the venting sequence.
whenToCallPro: Pressure switch or inducer service is usually needed.

title: Trane Furnace Code 4 Flashes: Open Limit Switch
meaning: The primary limit switch opened during the heating cycle.
whenToCallPro: Repeated limit trips need blower or limit switch replacement.

title: Trane Furnace Code 5 Flashes: Flame Detected When Off
meaning: The control sensed flame without a call for heat.
whenToCallPro: Unexpected flame requires immediate professional inspection.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.

title: Trane Furnace Code 6 Flashes: Line Voltage Out of Range
meaning: Supply voltage to the furnace was too high or too low.
diySteps: Note whether lights dim when the furnace runs.
Contact an electrician if voltage issues are suspected.
whenToCallPro: Persistent voltage faults need electrical diagnosis.

title: Trane Furnace Code 7 Flashes: Gas Valve Circuit Error
meaning: The gas valve circuit failed an electrical check.
whenToCallPro: Gas valve electrical faults require licensed service.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.

title: Trane Furnace Code 8 Flashes: Ignition Failure
meaning: The furnace failed to establish flame within the trial period.
diySteps: Reset and watch one ignition attempt.
whenToCallPro: Ignition failures usually need ignitor or flame sensor service.

title: Trane Furnace Code 9 Flashes: High-Stage Pressure Fault
meaning: The high-stage pressure switch did not respond correctly on two-stage units.
whenToCallPro: Two-stage pressure faults need switch or inducer diagnosis.

title: Trane Furnace Code 10 Flashes: Grounding Fault
meaning: The control detected a grounding or polarity problem.
diySteps: Do not operate until wiring is verified.
whenToCallPro: Grounding issues should be corrected by a qualified technician.

title: Trane Furnace Code 11 Flashes: Blower Motor Fault
meaning: The blower motor did not respond to the control signal.
diySteps: Spin the blower wheel to check for binding.
whenToCallPro: Blower motor or capacitor replacement is typically required.

title: Trane Furnace Code 12 Flashes: Inducer Motor Fault
meaning: The inducer motor failed during the pre-purge cycle.
whenToCallPro: Inducer motor replacement is needed if it will not start.

title: Trane Furnace Code 13 Flashes: Flame Rollout Trip
meaning: The rollout switch opened due to abnormal flame pattern.
whenToCallPro: Rollout conditions require combustion safety inspection.
dangerNote: If you smell gas or see soot, leave the area and call a technician.

title: Trane Furnace Code 14 Flashes: Ignitor Circuit Fault
meaning: The ignitor circuit failed a continuity or timing check.
whenToCallPro: Replace a failed ignitor or call for board diagnosis.

title: Trane Furnace Code 15 Flashes: Flame Sensor Fault
meaning: The flame sensor signal was out of range after ignition.
whenToCallPro: Replace the flame sensor if cleaning does not restore signal.

title: Trane Furnace Code 16 Flashes: Control Board Fault
meaning: The integrated control failed an internal self-test.
diySteps: Inspect the board area for moisture.
whenToCallPro: Control board replacement is usually required.

title: Trane Furnace Code 17 Flashes: Low Flame Lockout
meaning: The flame signal dropped too low during sustained operation.
whenToCallPro: Low flame lockouts need gas pressure and venting checks.

title: Trane Furnace Code 18 Flashes: Reverse Polarity
meaning: Line and neutral may be reversed at the furnace disconnect.
diySteps: Do not operate until polarity is corrected.
whenToCallPro: Have an electrician or HVAC tech verify line voltage wiring.
